sentence: This project uses deep learning on neuroimaging datasets to find differences between Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementias in each person’s connectome.
This project develops combination treatments to make immune checkpoint inhibitors delivered by platelets work better against triple-negative breast cancer.
This project builds a tool that pairs bacteriophages with their bacterial hosts using single-cell transcriptomics, to help study how phages and bacteria interact.
This project develops an RNA liquid biopsy platform to identify extracellular RNA markers of the hematopoietic lineage in blood.
This project studies how work-related stress affects sleep in Black and White adults, using self-reports, actigraphy, blood pressure monitoring and biomarkers.
This project builds a system that grows brain organoids, adds drugs or toxins, and measures changes in brain activity for drug screening.
This project studies non-prescribed stimulant use for neuropathic pain among people living with HIV.
This project tests whether synthetic exosomes carrying CRISPR can edit the apolipoprotein E4 gene in the brains of mice used to model Alzheimer’s disease.
This project studies how macrophages and Klebsiella pneumoniae interact during bacteremia, to find pathways that future therapies could target.
This project tries to find out how targeting a gene in the adult brain could reverse effects of its early loss on social cognition.
This project studies enzymes from several apicomplexan parasites that make phosphatidylcholine, to understand how they work at the molecular level.
This project builds a mobile health platform that gives manual wheelchair users with spinal cord injuries personalized guidance to lower pressure ulcer risk.
This project tests what gene regulatory elements and their variants do in the human genome across different biological contexts.
This project tries to find out whether the integrated stress response helps acute myeloid leukemia develop and get worse.
This project studies how archaeal cells sense mechanical forces, such as shear flow and compression, and turn them into biochemical responses.
This project compares mouse models of benign prostatic hyperplasia with human tissue by reading RNA in single cells, to see which match the disease.
This project develops machine learning methods to analyze cluster randomized trials of HIV prevention strategies despite missing data.
This project images single bacterial cells continuously to test how rare cells that survive antibiotics respond to antibiotics being designed.
This project tests whether boosting a signaling pathway can restore the function of aged blood stem cells.
This project carries out cancer research on prevention, screening and care coordination to improve cancer outcomes for members of Tribal Nations.
